Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 30. • Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
What is characterised as a free good?

options.A: one that has zero opportunity cost
options.B: one that is non-excludable and non-rivalrous
options.C: one that is supplied by the government with no charge
options.D: one that receives a 100% government subsidy

questions.questionText: A country is moving from a planned economy to a market economy. The government previously provided transport services but has now sold these to private firms. What is a consequence of this?

options.A: Government ownership of resources has increased.
options.B: Services provided by the public sector have increased.
options.C: There has been an increase in central planning.
options.D: There has been an increase in consumer sovereignty.

questions.questionText: A government wants to prevent the spread of an infectious disease by vaccinating all children. Why might vaccination be classified as a merit good?

options.A: The benefit to society is equal to the benefit received by the individual.
options.B: The good is excludable.
options.C: The good is not vital.
options.D: The good would otherwise be under-consumed.

questions.questionText: A product has a downward-sloping demand curve and an upward-sloping supply curve. What would explain a rise in the price of the product and a fall in the quantity of the product sold?

options.A: The decrease in demand is double the decrease in supply.
options.B: The decrease in supply is double the decrease in demand.
options.C: The increase in demand is double the increase in supply.
options.D: The increase in supply is double the increase in demand.

questions.questionText: Public transport in an economy has an income elasticity of demand of –0.36. What does this mean about public transport?

options.A: It has close substitutes.
options.B: It is a necessity.
options.C: It is a normal good.
options.D: It is an inferior good.

questions.questionText: The quantity demanded of a product is given by Q = 400 – 10P, when P is the price in dollars. D Supply of the product is fixed at 100 units. If the price is $20, what will be the position in the market?

options.A: It will be in disequilibrium with excess demand of 100 units.
options.B: It will be in disequilibrium with excess supply of 100 units.
options.C: It will be in equilibrium with 100 units traded.
options.D: It will be in equilibrium with 200 units traded.

A good has a unitary price elasticity of demand and at a price of $20 a firm sells 40000 units. How many units will the firm sell if it charges a price of $5?

A bus journey is considered an inferior good in a relatively rich country such as Singapore but a normal good in a relatively poor country such as Tanzania. In which direction would an increase in incomes in both countries cause the demand curve for bus journeys in Singapore and Tanzania to shift? Singapore Tanzania

options.A: left left
options.B: left right
options.C: right left
options.D: right right

questions.questionText: The quantity of a good supplied by a firm is Q. Each of these goods sells for a price of P. The area under the supply curve for Q goods is equal to C. What is the producer surplus of the firm?

options.A: P – C B P × Q C (P × Q) – C D (P – C) × Q

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market demand for and supply of good E. price of good E S Y X D D O quantity of good E The equilibrium has changed from X to Y. Which statement is not correct?

options.A: Incomes of consumers may have increased and good E is a normal good.
options.B: The quantity supplied has risen because price has increased.
options.C: The quantity supplied has risen because the production of good E has been subsidised.
options.D: The price of good F, which is a substitute for good E, may have risen.

A government regards alcoholic drinks as a demerit good and introduces a minimum price above the equilibrium in an attempt to protect consumers. Demand for alcoholic drinks is price inelastic. What is the most likely outcome?

options.A: a fall in the revenue of alcoholic drink producers
options.B: a fall in the quantity of alcoholic drink sales
options.C: a long-run shortage of alcoholic drinks
options.D: an increase in specific tax revenue from the sale of alcoholic drinks

questions.questionText: A government subsidy of $50 per unit is paid to manufacturers of solar panels. What will be the impact of this?

options.A: It will guarantee equilibrium in the solar panel market.
options.B: It will maintain high market prices.
options.C: It will reduce total production costs.
options.D: It will stabilise levels of output.

questions.questionText: Why might a government privatise the railway industry in a country?

options.A: Economists classify railway journeys as a public good.
options.B: Privatisation would provide funds for investment from a wider range of sources.
options.C: Privatised railways would be run to maximise producer surplus.
options.D: Railway fares can be taxed to raise money for the government only if railways are privatised.

questions.questionText: Which tax is levied on a stock of wealth rather than a flow of income?

options.A: company profits tax
options.B: goods and services (expenditure) tax
options.C: individual direct tax
options.D: personal asset tax

questions.questionText: What is classified as a transfer payment?

options.A: money paid as a gift to a charity
options.B: money paid as a tip to a waiter
options.C: money paid as commission to a salesperson
options.D: money paid for an imported good

questions.questionText: Under which circumstance would the rate of inflation be most likely to fall?

options.A: Government spending increases and society’s marginal propensity to save falls.
options.B: Reduced interest rates result in consumers increasing their spending.
options.C: The government increases direct taxes and the level of investment falls.
options.D: The prices of imported raw materials rise, whilst demand for exports falls.

questions.questionText: In which circumstances will country X have a comparative advantage in the production of rice over country Y?

options.A: when X has lower opportunity costs in producing rice than Y
options.B: when X is in a customs union and Y is outside that union
options.C: when X uses dollars for trading and Y uses a different currency
options.D: when X uses more units of labour than Y to produce rice

What is indicated by an economy’s terms of trade?

options.A: the degree of its dependence on imports
options.B: the international competitiveness of its exports
options.C: the purchasing power of its exports relative to its imports
options.D: the relative strength of its currency in the foreign exchange market

questions.questionText: A country operates a floating exchange rate. Why might a government change to a fixed exchange rate?

options.A: to increase the stock of foreign currency reserves
options.B: to make the terms of trade more favourable
options.C: to raise the level of certainty for businesses
options.D: to use the exchange rate to reduce domestic prices

questions.questionText: What term relates to a fall in the domestic real value of a currency?

options.A: deflation
options.B: depreciation
options.C: devaluation
options.D: inflation

questions.questionText: A country has a persistent balance of payments deficit. What is most likely to improve the situation in the long run?

options.A: a lowering of the level of import duties
options.B: a reduction in the level of income tax
options.C: the introduction of expansionary monetary policy
options.D: the use of grants to encourage new investment by firms

questions.questionText: To counter deflation a central bank uses expansionary monetary policy. What is likely to result?

options.A: a higher cost of borrowing
options.B: a higher rate of inflation
options.C: an appreciation of the exchange rate
options.D: an increase in government debt

questions.questionText: A government reduces the benefits that it pays to unemployed workers to increase the incentive to work. Which types of macroeconomic policies are being used? fiscal monetary supply-side policy policy policy

Suppose a country has a rate of inflation well below its target rate, high unemployment and a large balance of payments deficit. What would an economic advisor to the government be most likely to recommend?

options.A: a long-run supply-side policy, aimed at improving the country’s efficiency, so improving both the unemployment and the balance of payments positions
options.B: a revaluation of its currency, because that would lead to reduced unemployment and an improved balance of payments
options.C: a rise in interest rates, because it would lead to an improved balance of payments and help achieve the inflation target
options.D: a rise in levels of direct taxation, because that would improve unemployment and move inflation in the direction of a target level

questions.questionText: Country X is an open economy with a fixed exchange rate. Which combination of fiscal and monetary policies would be most effective in solving deflation? fiscal policy monetary policy

options.A: lower direct taxes devaluation
options.B: lower direct taxes revaluation
options.C: lower indirect taxes devaluation
